text:
Olivia - Support: pinging the thread — Acme reported repeat failures from our rerank endpoint when they pass precomputed embeddings from their pipeline. They say the API returns a 400 with a weird message. Copying error from them below.

Carlos - Acme (customer): hey team, this started after we switched our embed model to open-embed-768. Rerank call used to work with your hosted embedding model. now we get: `InvalidEmbeddingDim: expected 1024 but got 768` on /v1/rerank. Any quick fix?

Olivia - Support: thanks @Carlos. can you paste the exact payload (sanitized keys) and the rerank model you're calling? also, roughly how many candidates per request and batch size?

Carlos - Acme (customer): payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "query_embedding": [0.001, 0.23, ... 768 values ...],
  "candidate_embeddings": [[... 768 values ...], [...]],
  "model": "rwd-rerank-v1",
  "top_k": 10
}
```
we send ~20 candidates per query.

Ethan - SupportEng: ok this smells like an embedding-dim mismatch — our rerank models expect 1024-d vectors for rwd-rerank-v1. If they're submitting 768-d vectors (from open-embed-768) the server validation should return that error. Two questions: did they ever run embeddings via our /v1/embeddings endpoint previously (i.e., same model) or are they mixing an external embedder?

Carlos - Acme (customer): yes we switched to open-embed-768 to save cost/latency. We precompute and store vectors in our DB and then call your rerank to get final ordering. Worked before when we used rwd-embed-1024.

Maya - ML Eng: confirming — rwd-rerank-v1 (the ranking head) was trained and expects 1024-d inputs. There are three classes of fixes: 1) re-embed with a compatible model (recommended), 2) convert 768->1024 via a mapper (learned or padded) — risky, may change scores, 3) use a rerank model variant trained for 768 dims if available.

Sam - SRE: there's an operational nuance: the endpoint currently validates dims and rejects mismatches (that's what gave the 400). I can temporarily add a permissive path to accept different dims and route to an offline batch job that rescales, but that would be a risky live change. Would rather provide clear repro and recommended fixes first.

Olivia - Support: Carlos, short-term workaround: you can compute cosine similarity client-side between your query embedding and stored candidates and use that to approximate ranking until you re-run embeddings. If you want us to accept 768-d temporarily we'll need an RFC and eng signoff. Are you blocked for production traffic?

Carlos - Acme (customer): blocked on a rollout for next week. client-side cosine is okay but we'd lose the rerank model's fine-grained signals. Any chance of an automated adapter on our side?

Ethan - SupportEng: we can provide a quick adapter script that upcasts 768->1024 by zero-padding or by applying a learned linear projection if you have a small mapping dataset. Here's a naive zero-pad example for node/python:
```js
// naive pad to 1024
function padTo1024(vec){
  if(vec.length===1024) return vec;
  const pad = new Array(1024-vec.length).fill(0.0);
  return vec.concat(pad);
}
```
This will let the rerank API accept the payload but scores may shift.

Maya - ML Eng: adding detail — zero-padding preserves relative cosine in the original subspace (norm changes), but the reranker was trained on 1024 with particular tokenization/quantization characteristics. A linear projection trained on a small sample of (open-embed-768 -> rwd-embed-1024) pairs will be much better. We can prototype a least-squares mapper if Acme can provide ~2k example pairs.

Carlos - Acme (customer): we can do that. can you send a sample script for generating pairs? also curious if there's any billing/auth impact here — we precompute embeddings offline so we don't hit your embeddings endpoint often.

Ava - Billing: nothing changes in billing for rerank vs embeddings unless you call the embeddings endpoint. If you use our hosted embeddings instead of external, you'll be charged per embedding call. Precomputing on your infra avoids that. If you choose to re-embed with rwd-embed-1024, let us know and we can provide volume pricing.

Ethan - SupportEng: repro steps we used on our side: 1) Take a sample DB entry with 768-d vector. 2) Call /v1/rerank with that vector as query_embedding and candidate_embeddings -> observe 400 with body: `{"error":"InvalidEmbeddingDim", "details": "expected 1024, got 768"}`. 3) Pad vectors to 1024 and resubmit -> 200 OK and scores return. 4) Compare ordering delta. I attached a small script to reproduce (inline):
```bash
# curl repro (sanitized)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-rerank-v1","query_embedding":[0.01, ... 768 dims ...],"candidate_embeddings":[[...],[...]],"top_k":5}'
```
Response: `400 Bad Request` with JSON `{ "error": "InvalidEmbeddingDim", "details": "expected 1024, got 768" }`.

rerank-bot: automated note: ticket #SR-2247 linked. Please update ticket when resolved.

Maya - ML Eng: next steps from ML side: we can either 1) add a 768-d variant of the reranker (requires training + eval — ~2-4 weeks), or 2) provide a small projection model and a script (1-3 business days) that Acme can run locally to map 768->1024. If they can supply ~2k mapping examples we'll prefer to train a projection, otherwise we can give the naive pad script.

Olivia - Support: I'll coordinate with Acme on mapping examples. @Maya can you put together a small mapper PR (python + weights) we can share? @Sam please hold off on any permissive endpoint changes for now.

Sam - SRE: ack. won't touch prod validation. If we decide to host a mapper as a managed adapter, we'll need infra + cost estimate.

Carlos - Acme (customer): appreciate the quick responses. we'll export 2k pairs and drop into the ticket. also FYI we saw one auth transient earlier (401) when our token rotated — unrelated but wanted to flag.

Olivia - Support: noted — if you can upload pairs to the SR-2247, we'll triage and loop back with mapper + guidance. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
